Description: Alatheus served in 374 AD as regent commander and premier cavalry warlord of the Greuthungian (Ostrogothic) Amali dynasty, co-guarding the child-king Viderich alongside Saphrax. Stepping into the catastrophic vacuum left by Ermanaric's death and the fall of Vinitharius, Alatheus held the shattered Gothic nation together with iron fortitude. Coordinating closely with his Alan cavalry counterpart, he directed a masterclass in fighting retreats, using massive wagon-laagers to repel relentless Hunnic pursuit across hundreds of miles to the Lower Danube. Amidst the primeval forests and wind-swept Danubian plains, he held fast to the sacred warrior oaths and blood-brotherhood of the Gothic comitatus. A master of wagon-laager barricades and disciplined spear-shield walls, he fought at the forefront of the battle line, wielding broadaxe and spatha to smash enemy defenses. Enforcing strict battlefield solidarity among tribal youths, he regarded abandoning one's warband brother as unforgivable dishonor before the ancestral spirits. This rugged Germanic chieftain prized steel above gold, determined to carve a sovereign sanctuary for his people through the cataclysm of the Migration Period.

Motivations: Maintain impenetrable wagon-laager defenses against Hunnic pursuit to escort the young king safely to the Danube
Secure rich western plains for the reconstitution of the Ostrogothic cataphract hosts
Values: While the Amali bloodline breathes and shields hold, the Gothic nation is unbroken
The wagon-ring is life itself; iron discipline alone leads our people through the inferno to survival
Fears: Fears torrential autumn rains turning the steppe into impassable mud, immobilizing the defensive wagon-train
